title: a function invoked where it is written runs where it is written: a host read inside an immediately-invoked initializer is part of the pinned graph and adds no hop to the route
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Native Pin' (complete transitive graph, and the SHOULD sentence about the dependency path) and specification/requirements.mdx, 'Platform Requirements' (portability from the satisfied dependency closure). This case is 21-native-pin/a-host-read-in-a-module-initializer-is-part-of-the-pinned-graph with the read moved inside a function that is called on the spot, and the two DECLARE THE SAME ROUTE on purpose. That is the whole contract: `(() => process.pid)()` runs exactly when `process.pid` would have, so a walk that treats a function expression as deferred certifies one of these programs and refuses the other although they load the same module and run the same read; and the immediately-invoked callable is anonymous, so it must contribute no hop of its own between the binding and the read. `messageContains` therefore pins BOTH halves at once: the requirement is charged, and the route is `#pid -> process.pid` with nothing between them. The SMITHERS1601 companion is 20-host-globals/host-globals-are-unavailable's rule at the ambient read, declared rather than filtered because a cascade the language really does produce is part of the contract. Both backends refuse it today, so this case pins current behaviour on both rather than reproducing a live one-sided defect.
